title: 64. Numeracy & Number Systems: Division in Scientific Notation
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Divide two numbers in scientific notation with positive exponents.
questions.question: Divide \((6 \times 10^5) \div (2 \times 10^2)\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents: \(6 \div 2 = 3\), and \(10^5 \div 10^2 = 10^{5-2} = 10^3\). Therefore, \((6 \times 10^5) \div (2 \times 10^2) = 3 \times 10^3\). The alternative adds the exponents instead of subtracting them.
questions.hint: Divide the numbers in front and subtract the exponent of the divisor from the exponent of the dividend.

questions.learningObjective: Divide two numbers in scientific notation and keep the result in standard scientific notation.
questions.question: Divide \((8 \times 10^7) \div (4 \times 10^2)\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(8 \div 4 = 2\). Subtract the exponents: \(7-2=5\). Thus, \((8 \times 10^7) \div (4 \times 10^2) = 2 \times 10^5\). The alternative adds the exponents instead of subtracting them.

questions.learningObjective: Divide numbers in scientific notation and adjust the coefficient into standard form.
questions.question: Divide \((1.2 \times 10^8) \div (3 \times 10^2)\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(1.2 \div 3 = 0.4\). Subtract the exponents: \(8-2=6\). So the result is \(0.4 \times 10^6\). Rewrite \(0.4 \times 10^6\) as \(4 \times 10^5\). Therefore, the answer is \(4 \times 10^5\). The alternative normalizes the coefficient without decreasing the exponent.
questions.hint: After dividing, make sure the coefficient is at least \(1\) and less than \(10\).

questions.concept: Dividing Scientific Notation with Negative Exponents
questions.learningObjective: Divide numbers in scientific notation with negative exponents.
questions.question: Divide \((6.3 \times 10^{-4}) \div (9 \times 10^{-7})\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(6.3 \div 9 = 0.7\). Subtract the exponents: \(-4 - (-7) = -4 + 7 = 3\). So the result is \(0.7 \times 10^3\). Rewrite \(0.7 \times 10^3\) as \(7 \times 10^2\). Therefore, the answer is \(7 \times 10^2\). The alternative normalizes the coefficient without decreasing the exponent.
questions.hint: Subtracting a negative exponent is the same as adding its opposite.

questions.concept: Dividing Scientific Notation with Negative Exponents
questions.learningObjective: Divide numbers in scientific notation and adjust the result when the coefficient is less than 1.
questions.question: Divide \((2.4 \times 10^{-3}) \div (6 \times 10^{-5})\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(2.4 \div 6 = 0.4\). Subtract the exponents: \(-3 - (-5) = -3 + 5 = 2\). So the result is \(0.4 \times 10^2\). Rewrite \(0.4 \times 10^2\) as \(4 \times 10^1\). Therefore, the answer is \(4 \times 10^1\). The alternative normalizes the coefficient without decreasing the exponent.
questions.hint: Write the quotient as \(a\times10^n\) with \(1\le a<10\).

questions.learningObjective: Divide numbers in scientific notation when the coefficient quotient is less than 1.
questions.question: Divide \((5.4 \times 10^6) \div (9 \times 10^2)\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(5.4 \div 9 = 0.6\). Subtract the exponents: \(6-2=4\). So the result is \(0.6 \times 10^4\). Rewrite \(0.6 \times 10^4\) as \(6 \times 10^3\). Therefore, the answer is \(6 \times 10^3\). The alternative normalizes the coefficient without decreasing the exponent.
questions.hint: If the coefficient is less than \(1\), move one factor of \(10\) from the exponent to the coefficient.

questions.concept: Dividing with Negative and Positive Exponents
questions.learningObjective: Divide a number with a negative exponent by a number with a positive exponent.
questions.question: Divide \((3.5 \times 10^{-2}) \div (7 \times 10^3)\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(3.5 \div 7 = 0.5\). Subtract the exponents: \(-2 - 3 = -5\). So the result is \(0.5 \times 10^{-5}\). Rewrite \(0.5 \times 10^{-5}\) as \(5 \times 10^{-6}\). Therefore, the answer is \(5 \times 10^{-6}\). The alternative normalizes the coefficient without decreasing the exponent.
questions.hint: Subtract the exponent in the denominator from the exponent in the numerator.

questions.concept: Dividing Scientific Notation with Decimal Coefficients
questions.learningObjective: Divide numbers in scientific notation with decimal coefficients.
questions.question: Divide \((8.4 \times 10^5) \div (2.1 \times 10^2)\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(8.4 \div 2.1 = 4\). Subtract the exponents: \(5-2=3\). Therefore, \((8.4 \times 10^5) \div (2.1 \times 10^2) = 4 \times 10^3\). The alternative adds the exponents instead of subtracting them.
questions.hint: Divide the decimal coefficients carefully, then subtract the exponents.

questions.concept: Dividing Scientific Notation with Negative Exponents
questions.learningObjective: Divide numbers in scientific notation with negative exponents and adjust the coefficient.
questions.question: Divide \((1.5 \times 10^{-4}) \div (5 \times 10^{-6})\).
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients: \(1.5 \div 5 = 0.3\). Subtract the exponents: \(-4 - (-6) = -4 + 6 = 2\). So the result is \(0.3 \times 10^2\). Rewrite \(0.3 \times 10^2\) as \(3 \times 10^1\). Therefore, the answer is \(3 \times 10^1\). The alternative normalizes the coefficient without decreasing the exponent.
questions.hint: Handle the negative exponents by subtracting, then adjust the coefficient if needed.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a real-world problem by dividing numbers written in scientific notation.
questions.question: A sample contains \(7.2 \times 10^8\) bacteria in \(2.4 \times 10^2\text{ mL}\). How many bacteria are there per mL? Write the answer in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: Divide the total number of bacteria by the volume: \((7.2 \times 10^8) \div (2.4 \times 10^2)\). Divide the coefficients: \(7.2 \div 2.4 = 3\). Subtract the exponents: \(8-2=6\). Therefore, the number of bacteria per mL is \(3 \times 10^6\). The alternative adds the volume exponent instead of subtracting it.
questions.hint: Use division of scientific notation: divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents.
